toolColorblind.aboutContent:
What Is the Colorblind Simulator?

The Colorblind Simulator is a free online accessibility tool that shows you how any color palette appears to people with different types of color vision deficiency (CVD). By previewing your designs through the lens of protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, and achromatopsia, you can identify problematic color choices before they reach your audience.

Approximately 8% of men and 0.5% of women worldwide have some form of color vision deficiency. That means roughly 1 in 12 male users may perceive your interface, chart, or illustration differently than you intended. If critical information is communicated through color alone — red for errors, green for success — colorblind users may miss it entirely.

This tool is essential for UI/UX designers validating design systems, data-visualization engineers ensuring chart legibility, game designers testing HUD elements, and marketers checking brand assets. Testing early prevents costly redesigns later.

  • Simulates protanopia (red-blind), deuteranopia (green-blind), tritanopia (blue-blind), and achromatopsia (total color blindness)
  • Side-by-side comparison of original and simulated palettes
  • Edit colors directly and see simulated results in real time
  • No uploads required — all processing happens in your browser
toolColorblind.howToContent:
How to Use the Colorblind Simulator

Testing your palette for colorblind accessibility is fast and straightforward.

  1. Enter your palette — The tool displays a default palette. Click any swatch to change it to one of your project colors using the color picker or by pasting a HEX code.
  2. Review the simulation panel — Below your original palette, the tool shows four simulated versions: Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, and Achromatopsia. Each version shows how your colors appear to someone with that condition.
  3. Compare original and simulated — Look for colors that merge together or become indistinguishable in any simulation. These are problem areas where colorblind users may lose information.
  4. Adjust problematic colors — Click on the original swatch of any problematic color and shift its hue, saturation, or lightness until the simulated versions remain distinguishable from neighboring swatches.
  5. Reset if needed — Click Reset to return all swatches to the default palette and start fresh.
  6. Iterate — Repeat the process until your palette passes a visual check in all four simulation types.

Best practice: never rely on color alone to convey meaning. Supplement color with icons, labels, patterns, or varying thickness to ensure information is accessible regardless of vision type.

The URL Color Extractor is a free online tool that fetches the HTML and CSS of any public website and identifies every color value used in its design. It gives designers, developers, and brand analysts a complete inventory of a site's color palette without opening developer tools or inspecting stylesheets manually.

Understanding how other websites use color is valuable for competitive analysis, redesign planning, brand auditing, and educational research. A single webpage may reference dozens of unique colors across backgrounds, text, borders, shadows, and gradients. This tool collects them all and presents them as a clean, sortable palette.

Typical users include UX researchers benchmarking competitor interfaces, front-end developers auditing legacy codebases for color consolidation, brand managers verifying that a third-party agency followed brand guidelines, and students studying real-world design patterns.

  • Analyzes HTML inline styles and up to five linked CSS files

toolUrl.howToContent:
How to Use the URL Color Extractor

Extract a complete color inventory from any website in three simple steps.

toolDarkTheme.aboutContent:
What Is the Dark Theme Generator?

The Dark Theme Generator is a free online tool that creates a complete, harmonious dark-mode color palette from a single accent color. It outputs background shades, surface colors, text tones, and accent variations — everything you need to implement a professional dark theme in your application or website.

Dark mode has evolved from a niche preference to a mainstream expectation. Users appreciate reduced eye strain in low-light environments, lower battery consumption on OLED screens, and the modern aesthetic that dark interfaces provide. However, designing an effective dark theme is harder than simply inverting colors. Backgrounds need subtle variation to create depth, text must maintain sufficient contrast, and accent colors must pop without overwhelming.

This tool handles all of that automatically. Product designers use it to prototype dark-mode variants of their design systems, front-end developers generate CSS-ready palettes for dark theme toggles, and indie hackers ship polished dark UIs without hiring a designer.

  • Generates a full palette from one accent color
  • Multiple preset styles for different moods
  • Adjustable contrast level
  • Live preview with realistic UI components
toolDarkTheme.howToContent:
How to Use the Dark Theme Generator

Create a complete dark theme palette in seconds by following these steps.

  1. Pick an accent color — Use the Accent Color picker to select your brand's primary color or any hue you want as the focal point of your dark theme.
  2. Choose a preset — Browse the Presets to select a dark-theme style. Each preset adjusts background warmth, surface elevation, and text brightness to create a distinct mood.
  3. Adjust contrast — Use the Contrast slider to control how much separation exists between background layers and text. Higher contrast improves readability; lower contrast creates a more subtle, immersive feel.
  4. Preview the theme — The live preview panel renders a sample dashboard interface using your generated palette. Check how cards, buttons, text, and backgrounds work together.
  5. Randomize — Click Randomize to generate a completely new accent color and see a different theme variation instantly.
  6. Copy or export — Click individual color swatches to copy HEX values, or use the export feature to download the full palette as CSS variables, Tailwind config, or other formats.

Tip: test your dark theme palette with the Contrast Checker to verify that text-on-background combinations meet WCAG AA or AAA standards.

toolSvgColor.aboutContent:
What Is the SVG Color Editor?

The SVG Color Editor is a free online tool that lets you upload any SVG file, automatically detects every color used in its paths, shapes, and styles, and provides a visual interface to change those colors instantly. The modified SVG can then be downloaded, ready to use in your project.

SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is the standard format for icons, logos, illustrations, and infographics on the web. Unlike raster images, SVGs use code to describe shapes, which means their colors are defined as attributes and CSS properties that can be edited. However, manually editing SVG XML is tedious, error-prone, and impractical for complex files with dozens of color values.

This tool makes SVG recoloring accessible to everyone — not just developers comfortable with code. Graphic designers rebrand icon sets in minutes, marketers adapt illustrations to campaign themes, and developers quickly adjust open-source SVG assets to match their application's design system.

  • Automatic detection of all fill, stroke, and style colors
  • Visual color picker for each detected color
  • Side-by-side original and modified preview
  • Download the modified SVG with one click
toolSvgColor.howToContent:
How to Use the SVG Color Editor

Recoloring an SVG file takes just a few clicks. Follow these steps to upload, edit, and export.

  1. Upload an SVG — Drag and drop an SVG file onto the dropzone, or click to browse your files. The tool accepts standard .svg files.
  2. View detected colors — The tool scans the SVG's markup and lists every unique color found in fill, stroke, and inline style attributes. Each color appears as an editable swatch.
  3. Edit colors — Click any color swatch to open the color picker. Choose a new color and the SVG preview updates in real time.
  4. Compare original and modified — Toggle between the Original and Modified tabs to see a before/after comparison of your changes.
  5. Randomize — Click the Random button to apply a random color transformation to all detected colors for creative exploration.
  6. Reset — Click Reset to revert all color changes back to the original SVG values.
  7. Download — Click Download SVG to save the modified file to your computer. The downloaded file retains all original structure and attributes with only the colors changed.
  8. Upload another — Click Upload New to start over with a different SVG file.

Tip: for best results, use SVGs where colors are defined as fill and stroke attributes rather than embedded raster images or complex CSS classes.

toolTailwindColors.aboutContent:
What Is the Tailwind Colors Preview?

The Tailwind Colors Preview is a free online tool that generates a complete Tailwind CSS color scale (50 through 950) from a single base color, then previews those colors on realistic UI components so you can see exactly how they will look in a real application. It bridges the gap between picking a color and understanding its impact on production interfaces.

Tailwind CSS uses a numbered shade system where each color has eleven variants ranging from very light (50) to very dark (950). Getting this scale right is critical: too little contrast between steps makes the shades indistinguishable, while too much contrast creates jarring jumps. Our algorithm generates perceptually balanced scales that integrate seamlessly with Tailwind's default palette.

Front-end developers use this tool when adding custom brand colors to their Tailwind config. Designers use it to validate color choices against realistic UI patterns — buttons, cards, dashboards, pricing tables — before committing to a design system. Product managers use it to quickly mock up themed interfaces during planning sessions.

  • Generates full 50–950 shade scale from one base color
  • Live preview on buttons, cards, dashboards, and more
  • Copy individual shade values or export the full config
  • Named palette export for tailwind.config.js
toolTailwindColors.howToContent:
How to Use the Tailwind Colors Preview

Create and preview a complete Tailwind color scale in just a few steps.

  1. Pick a base color — Use the Base Color (500) picker to select your primary brand color. The 500 shade is the middle of the scale and typically your most-used variant.
  2. Name your palette — Enter a Palette Name (e.g., 'brand', 'primary', 'ocean') that will be used as the key in your Tailwind config export.
  3. Review the shade scale — The tool generates eleven shades from 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). Each swatch shows its number and HEX value.
  4. Preview on real components — Scroll down to the Examples section to see your color applied to realistic UI patterns: call-to-action cards, category pills, chat bubbles, schedules, statistics, pricing tables, and more.
  5. Randomize — Click Random to generate a completely new base color and see how a different palette transforms the preview components.
  6. Copy or export — Click Copy on any individual shade, or use the export panel to download the full scale as a Tailwind config snippet, CSS variables, SCSS, or JSON.

Tip: after generating your scale, test the 50/900 and 100/800 combinations with the Contrast Checker to ensure text on background meets WCAG AA standards across your shade spectrum.

faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Kolr

q1.question: What is Kolr?
q1.answer: Kolr is a free color palette generator and toolkit for designers, developers, and color enthusiasts. It helps you create, explore, and manage color palettes with tools like random generation, image extraction, gradient creation, and accessibility checking.

q2.question: Is Kolr free to use?
q2.answer: Yes! All web tools on Kolr are completely free to use with no account required. The mobile app is free to download with optional premium features.

q3.question: How does the random palette generator work?
q3.answer: Our random palette generator uses color theory algorithms to create harmonious 5-color palettes. It randomly selects from monochromatic, analogous, complementary, triadic, and tetradic harmony rules to ensure every palette looks great.

q4.question: How do I extract colors from an image?
q4.answer: Use our Image Color Extractor tool: upload any image and our algorithm will analyze the dominant colors and extract a 5-color palette. You can then copy individual hex codes or the entire palette.

q5.question: What is the contrast checker?
q5.answer: The contrast checker tests the color contrast ratio between two colors against WCAG accessibility standards. It shows whether your color combination meets AA and AAA requirements for both normal and large text.

q6.question: How does the gradient generator work?
q6.answer: The gradient generator lets you pick 2-4 colors and create linear, radial, or conic CSS gradients. You can adjust the angle, copy the CSS code, and use it directly in your projects.

q7.question: What color formats are supported?
q7.answer: Kolr works with HEX (#RRGGBB), RGB, and HSL color formats. Our tools can extract and convert between these formats automatically.

q8.question: Can I export my palettes?
q8.answer: Yes! You can export palettes as CSS variables, Tailwind config, SCSS variables, JSON, PNG images, and SVG files. Just use the export feature available on each tool page.

q9.question: Does Kolr save my palettes?
q9.answer: Your palette history is saved locally in your browser using localStorage. This means your data stays on your device and persists between sessions, but won't sync across different browsers or devices.

q10.question: Is the mobile app available on iOS and Android?
q10.answer: Yes! Kolr is available on both the App Store (iOS 13+) and Google Play (Android 8+). The mobile app includes additional features like camera-based color extraction.

q11.question: Does the app work offline?
q11.answer: Yes, the mobile app works fully offline. All color processing happens locally on your device, so you can create and save palettes without an internet connection.

q12.question: How is my privacy protected?
q12.answer: Kolr takes privacy seriously. Your photos are processed locally and never uploaded to any server. The web tools don't require any account or personal information. Read our full Privacy Policy for more details.

toolColorblindUrl.aboutContent:
What Is the Colorblind Website Checker?

The Colorblind Website Checker is a free online tool that loads any public website inside a simulated viewport and applies real-time color vision deficiency filters. It lets you see exactly how your live website — with all its images, text, buttons, and backgrounds — appears to users with protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, or achromatopsia.

While the palette-based Colorblind Simulator is great for checking isolated color swatches, real websites are far more complex. Colors interact with photographs, gradients overlap with text, and hover states change dynamically. This tool captures the full picture by rendering the actual site and applying CSS filter transformations that simulate each type of color vision deficiency.

Web designers, accessibility auditors, product managers, and QA engineers use this tool to validate that navigation cues, form states, call-to-action buttons, charts, and marketing banners remain effective for all users regardless of their color vision.

  • Live website rendering with colorblind simulation filters
  • Supports protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, and achromatopsia
  • Toggle between normal vision and each deficiency type
  • Direct link to open the original site for comparison
toolColorblindUrl.howToContent:
How to Use the Colorblind Website Checker

Test any live website for colorblind accessibility with these simple steps.

  1. Enter the URL — Paste the full website address (including https://) into the input field at the top of the tool.
  2. Click Load — The tool loads the website inside an embedded viewport. Some sites may block iframe embedding; if the site does not appear, try a different URL.
  3. Select a vision type — Choose from Normal, Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, or Achromatopsia using the filter buttons. The site re-renders instantly with the selected color filter.
  4. Inspect the result — Scroll through the simulated page and look for elements where color is the sole differentiator: navigation highlights, error messages, status indicators, chart legends, and button states.
  5. Switch between types — Click through each vision type to compare. Issues visible in one simulation may not appear in others.
  6. Open the original — Click Open Site to view the unfiltered page in a new tab, making side-by-side comparison easy.

Tip: pay special attention to red/green distinctions (protanopia and deuteranopia cover about 7% of males) and ensure that every interactive element has a non-color indicator such as an underline, icon, or label change.

toolCompare.aboutContent:
What Is Palette Compare?

Palette Compare is a free online tool that places two color palettes side by side so you can evaluate their differences, similarities, and overall harmony at a glance. It is the fastest way to compare a proposed redesign palette against the current brand colors, benchmark two competitor palettes, or decide between two mood-board options.

Choosing the right palette is rarely a one-shot decision. Designers iterate through multiple variations, stakeholders propose alternatives, and A/B tests require visual comparison. Without a dedicated comparison view, evaluating two palettes means switching tabs, squinting at screenshots, or relying on memory — all of which introduce bias and slow decision-making.

This tool eliminates that friction. Brand designers use it during guideline reviews, product teams use it when evaluating theme variants, and educators use it to teach color relationships by showing how two palettes overlap or diverge.

  • Side-by-side palette display with up to five colors each
  • Highlights shared colors across both palettes
  • Harmony analysis for each palette
  • Randomize either palette for quick exploration
toolCompare.howToContent:
How to Use Palette Compare

Comparing two palettes is simple and interactive. Follow these steps to get a clear side-by-side evaluation.

  1. Set Palette A — Click any swatch in the Palette A row to open the color picker and choose your first palette's colors. You can also paste HEX codes directly.
  2. Set Palette B — Do the same for the Palette B row. This could be an alternative design, a competitor's colors, or a randomly generated set.
  3. Randomize — Click the Randomize button on either palette to generate a new set of colors for quick comparison experiments.
  4. Review the comparison — The Comparison section shows both palettes stacked, making it easy to spot which colors are similar and which diverge.
  5. Check harmony — The Harmony indicator evaluates whether each palette follows a recognizable color-theory rule (analogous, complementary, etc.).
  6. Identify shared colors — The Shared section highlights any colors that appear in both palettes, helping you find common ground between two options.

Tip: use this tool during design reviews by loading the current production palette in A and the proposed update in B. It makes stakeholder discussions more objective and focused.

toolColorConverter.description: Instantly convert between HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH and CMYK
toolColorConverter.aboutContent:
What Is the Color Converter?

The Color Converter is a free online tool that instantly translates any color between five major formats: HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH, and CMYK. Paste or type a color value in any supported format and the tool displays the equivalent value in every other format simultaneously.

Color format conversion is a daily task for anyone working across design and development workflows. Designers often work in HSL for intuitive hue/saturation adjustments, while CSS code uses HEX or RGB. Print designers need CMYK values, and the newer OKLCH format offers perceptually uniform color manipulation for cutting-edge CSS. Switching between tools or doing manual math is time-consuming and error-prone.

This converter eliminates that friction. Front-end developers paste a HEX code from a Figma file and get the HSL equivalent for CSS custom properties. Print designers take an RGB brand color and find its CMYK approximation. Color scientists explore OKLCH values for perceptually linear gradients. All from one input field.

  • Supports HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH, and CMYK
  • Bidirectional conversion — enter in any format, get all others
  • Copy any output value with one click
  • No installation or sign-up required
toolColorConverter.howToContent:
How to Use the Color Converter

Converting between color formats takes just one step — type or paste, and the tool does the rest.

  1. Enter a color — Type or paste a color value into the input field. The tool accepts HEX (#FF5733), RGB (rgb(255,87,51)), HSL (hsl(14,100%,60%)), OKLCH (oklch(0.65 0.2 30)), and CMYK (cmyk(0,66,80,0)) formats.
  2. View all conversions — The tool instantly recognizes the input format and displays the equivalent value in all five formats: HEX, RGB, HSL, OKLCH, and CMYK.
  3. Copy a value — Click the copy icon next to any format to place its value on your clipboard.
  4. Try another color — Simply clear the input and enter a new value. The conversions update in real time as you type.
  5. Use the color picker — Alternatively, click the color swatch to open a visual color picker and select a color interactively. All format outputs update as you move through the picker.

Note on CMYK: the conversion to CMYK is a mathematical approximation. Actual print colors depend on the printer, ink, paper, and ICC profile. Always verify CMYK values with a proof before sending to production.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.subtitle: We believe color tools should be usable by everyone, regardless of ability
accessibility.commitDesc: Kolr is built with accessibility as a core value, not an afterthought. We follow WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines and go beyond compliance by providing a built-in accessibility widget that lets every user customize their experience. Our goal is to make color tools truly inclusive.
accessibility.widgetDesc: Every page includes a floating accessibility button (bottom left) with the following options:
accessibility.textSizeDesc: Increase text size to 120% or 140% for better readability across the entire site.
accessibility.contrastDesc: Boost contrast ratios with brighter text and stronger borders for improved visibility.
accessibility.motionDesc: Disable all transitions and animations for users sensitive to motion. Also respects your OS prefers-reduced-motion setting.
accessibility.colorblindDesc: Apply protanopia, deuteranopia, or tritanopia filters to preview the site as colorblind users see it.
accessibility.focusDesc: Bright yellow focus outlines on all interactive elements for easier keyboard navigation.
accessibility.cursorDesc: Enlarged cursor for users with motor difficulties or low vision.
accessibility.keyboardDesc: Every feature is accessible via keyboard. Tab to navigate, Enter to activate, Escape to close menus and dialogs.
accessibility.screenReaderDesc: Semantic HTML, ARIA labels, live regions, and descriptive alt text throughout the site for full screen reader compatibility.
accessibility.standard1: WCAG 2.1 AA compliant — contrast ratios meet 7:1 (AAA level)
accessibility.standard2: Semantic HTML with proper landmarks: nav, main, footer
accessibility.standard3: ARIA attributes on all interactive components (buttons, menus, tabs, dialogs)
accessibility.standard5: Focus trap in modals and mobile menu
accessibility.standard7: aria-live regions for dynamic content announcements
accessibility.standard8: Multi-language support (English & French) including accessibility features
